div.head: VI Atr 52.1
div.ab: ⁊ gif hit geweorþeð, þæt man unwilles oþþe ungewealdes ænig þing misdeð, na bið þæt na gelic þam þe willes ⁊ gewealdes sylfwilles misdeð; ⁊ eac se þe nydwyrhta bið þæs þe he misdeð, se bið gebeorhges ⁊ þy beteran domes symle wyrðe, þe he nydwyrhta wæs þæs þe he worhte.

⁊ gif hit geweorþeð, þæt man unwilles oþþe ungewealdes ænig þing misdeð, na bið þæt na gelic þam þe willes ⁊ gewealdes sylfwilles misdeð; ⁊ eac se þe nydwyrhta bið þæs þe he misdeð, se bið gebeorhges ⁊ þy beteran domes symle wyrðe, þe he nydwyrhta wæs þæs þe he worhte.

And gif hit geweorþeð þæt man unwilles oþþe ungewealdes ænig þing misdeð, na bið þæt na gelic þam þe willes and gewealdes sylfwilles misdeð: and eac se þe nydwyrhta bið þæs þe he misdeð, se bið gebeorhges and þy beteran domes symle wyrðe, þe he nydwyrhta wæs þæs þe he worhte.

Und wenn es vorkommt, dass jemand ohne Willen oder Absicht irgend eine Missethat verübt, so ist dies nicht gleich dem, der mit Willen und Absicht bewusst Missethat übt; und auch wer ein Ausführer dessen, was er verbricht, [nur] durch Zwang ist, der ist immer Schutzes werth und eines um so günstigeren Urtheils, als er [nur] durch Zwang Ausführer dessen, was er verübt hat, gewesen ist.

And if it happens that someone commits any misdeed involuntarily or unintentionally, that is not the same as one who does wrong wilfully and intentionally, of his own will; and also whoever is the doer of what he commits [only] under compulsion, he is always deserving of protection and of a more favourable judgment, in that he was [only] under compulsion the doer of what he did.

And if it happens that a man commits a misdeed, involuntarily or unintentionally, the case is different from that of one who offends of his own freewill, voluntarily and intentionally; and likewise he who is an involuntary agent in his misdeeds should always be entitled to clemency and to better terms, owing to the fact that he acted as an involuntary agent.

And if it befalls that someone commits a crime in any way unwillingly or unknowingly, that shall not be treated as if he intentionally committed a crime, willingly and knowingly; and accordingly, the person who is compelled so that he commits a crime is always to be deemed worthy of mercy and lighter judgments, because he acted out of compulsion.
